A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs describe the same knowledge-graph reasoning study. All 21 pages of v3 and 25 pages of v4, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Llama pretraining experiments on FB15K-237 and synthetic knowledge graphs, including reasoning accuracy, loss, ablations, and an empirical scaling fit.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their results in Figures 1, 3, and 4, alongside the appendix graph-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The Llama architecture, next-token training objective, graph-generation procedure, and multiple-choice inference remain unchanged. The appendix generation code matches; the new one-layer attention construction supports a theoretical argument rather than a changed experimental model.

E1.justification: Both versions use FB15K-237 and the same synthetic graph coverage. GPT-generated sentences, template sentences, random-ID triples, and the graph-property sweeps are retained without additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain between Llama sizes, training budgets, and data configurations. Newly cited benign-overfitting and state-space-model works are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v4 Section 3 introduces a best-checkpoint, epsilon-tolerant criterion for selecting the smallest sufficient model. Section 5.2 also revises the stationary weights used in graph search entropy. Tables 1–3 and the stated 10k-step empirical analysis remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns using these revisions.

E4.justification: Figure 3 retains the same six training-budget and graph-property ablations, and Figures 6–7 retain the graph-distribution comparisons. The rewritten discussion supplies no additional ablation, robustness experiment, or case study.

E5.justification: v4 newly describes stability 'across runs,' but does not clarify whether these are repeated trials of identical settings or different configurations, and supplies no counts or seeds. Figure 4 retains the same 95% confidence band, so an additional repeated-run reporting practice cannot be established.

E6.justification: All plotted results are retained, including R² = 0.85 and approximately 124 parameters per bit in Section 5.2. v4 Section 3 adds qualitative assertions of across-run stability and optimal performance with batch size 1024, without new numerical comparisons supporting those assertions.

T1.justification: v4 adds formal best-achievable-loss and optimal-size definitions, a convergence theorem, and a conditional-complexity scaling theorem with proof arguments in Appendices B–C. It also changes the stationary-distribution expression from psi_i/||psi||² to psi_i²/||psi||². These substantially expand and revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion shift from overparameterization harming reasoning toward identifying the smallest sufficient parameter budget, while allowing larger models to match performance. The scaling relationship is now claimed theoretically as well as empirically, and the approximate 0.008-bit estimate is presented as 'at most.'

C2.justification: v4 attributes the U-shaped behavior specifically to prolonged training and emphasizes that larger models can perform comparably at suitable checkpoints. It adds qualifications about semantic sharing and the Transformer-dependent upper bound. The original limitation concerning real-world text pretraining is retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v4 adds details about space-separated integer IDs and randomly sampled incorrect answer options. It removes v3's supplementary-notebook availability statement and explicit FB15K-237 epoch example, while retaining the code URL, generation listing, and experimental settings tables.

R1.justification: v4 adds Bartlett et al. (2020), Belkin et al. (2020), Gu et al. (2022), and Gu and Dao (2024), connecting its argument to benign overfitting, double descent, and architectural alternatives. Existing related-work coverage is largely retained, with a more explicit novelty assertion for graph search entropy.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around minimal sufficient capacity. Sections 2–3 are renamed and reorganized, ablation explanations become condensed bullets, limitations move to the appendix, and an impact statement replaces the reproducibility section.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures, equations, and captions. All seven figure assets and three tables retain their content, while appendix placement and page composition change.

improvement.justification: v4 usefully distinguishes sufficient capacity from overtraining, but upgrades the empirical relationship to central theoretical guarantees with unresolved proof steps. Appendix B absorbs an extra delta into a fixed epsilon; Appendix C.6 invokes undefined assumptions S1/S2 and moves from path entropy to endpoint entropy without establishing the connection. These rigor concerns, alongside unchanged quantitative evidence, prevent a reliable judgment that the clearer framing yields a net quality improvement.
